llm.reply:
Clinical trials retrieved for this search investigate interventions for thyroid cancer [1][2]. These registered studies evaluate targeted therapies, cytotoxic drugs, and radioimmunotherapy regimens [3][4][5].

## Clinical Trial Interventions
Evaluated therapeutic regimens include radioimmunotherapy with or without chemotherapy alongside peripheral stem cell transplantation [1]. Additional studies examine systemic agents including thalidomide, irinotecan, tanespimycin, and suberoylanilide hydroxamic acid [2][3][4][5].

## Pathology and Registry Context
Related biomedical records identify the concept Medullary Carcinoma, Not Otherwise Specified [7]. Epidemiological work cataloged under 15365566 analyzed morphology classifications in a population-based cohort [8][6]. Across these histological categories, 5-year relative survival was 66% for not otherwise specified carcinoma [9: "ranged from 66% (95% CI 61-71) for NOS carcinoma"].

Clinical trials relevant to this query include Radioimmunotherapy With or Without Chemotherapy Plus Peripheral Stem Cell Transplantation in Treating Patients With Thyroid Cancer [1]. Additional identified clinical studies investigate therapeutic options such as Thalidomide in Treating Patients With Thyroid Cancer [2].

## Clinical Trial Interventions
Evaluated interventions include Irinotecan in Treating Patients With Metastatic or Inoperable Thyroid Cancer [3]. Other protocols investigate Tanespimycin in Treating Patients With Inoperable Locoregionally Advanced or Metastatic Thyroid Cancer [4]. Further investigated approaches evaluate Suberoylanilide Hydroxamic Acid in Treating Patients With Metastatic and/or Locally Advanced or Locally Recurrent Thyroid Cancer [5].

## Classification And Characterization
A relevant classification concept is Medullary Carcinoma, Not Otherwise Specified [7]. 

## Prognostic Literature Evidence
Survival was examined in Prognostic value of morphology and hormone receptor status in breast cancer - a population-based study [6]. This investigation corresponds to publication pmid 15365566 [8]. Within this study population, relative survival at five years was lowest for NOS carcinoma among specified microscopic forms and highest for special types [9: "the 5-year relative survival ranged from 66% (95% CI 61-71) for NOS carcinoma to 95% (95% CI 90-100) for special types"]. Analysis confirmed that morphology and hormone receptor status remained significant prognostic variables following adjustment for age and diagnostic stage [9: "Morphology and hormone receptor status were confirmed as significant survival predictors in this population-based study, even after adjusting for age and stage at diagnosis"].
